name: TFT Positioning Guide (Mobalytics)
one_line: Guide covering frontline/backline layering and AOE-range item interactions in Teamfight Tactics
take_what: asymmetric tank placement: put the TANKIEST unit on the outside edge, not center, because enemy corner-parked carries route damage there first, and a stronger unit soaking the wrong-side attack stalls longer than a weak one would

name: TFT Carry Positioning (TFT Ninja)
one_line: Deep strategy page on corner-tucking carries, bodyguard tanks, and AI targeting exploits
take_what: corner placement mechanically halves attack surface: a unit in a grid corner can only be approached from 2-3 directions instead of up to 6/8, converting a spatial choice into a defensive stat without changing any number on the card

name: TFT Carry Positioning — bodyguard/targeting rule (TFT Ninja)
one_line: Same page: explains the 'units attack closest enemy, tank intercepts' mechanic that makes tank walls functional
take_what: units auto-target nearest enemy by default; placing a tank one hex closer to the enemy line than your carry guarantees the AI locks onto the tank first and 'wastes' its turn there — this is the single rule that makes frontline/backline exist as a concept at all
constraint: Limen has no combat-resolution AI (placement IS the action), so 'closest enemy targeting' would have to be reframed as adjacency-based capture range rather than auto-attack routing

name: TFT Ninja — AOE spread & assassin counter-positioning
one_line: Coverage of how corner defaults get punished by assassins (target-farthest) and Zephyr (banish), forcing reactive repositioning
take_what: a single 'always correct' default position (corner-tuck) becomes a trap once the metagame learns to punish it — design needs at least one counter-mechanic (farthest-target unit, displacement spell) that specifically inverts the safe spot, or positioning skill collapses into a solved formula
constraint: none — this is a caution, not a mechanic to port directly

name: Super Auto Pets Strategies Wiki
one_line: Line-based (not grid) autobattler where front/back slot order alone drives all combat resolution
take_what: positioning collapses to a single ordered line (5 slots) instead of 2D grid, and specific slot numbers (front=tankiest, slot 5=summon-on-faint/buff units) carry fixed roles — proves a much simpler 1D positioning space can still generate deep strategy
constraint: Limen is inherently 2D hex so this doesn't port directly, but the 'each slot has a canonical job' idea (edge tile vs. interior tile vs. capital-adjacent tile) could give hex positions similarly legible roles

name: Dota Underlords positioning guide — Zone of Control (BlueStacks)
one_line: Explains Underlords' 'zone of control' concept: a lone unit's threat radius covers the whole enemy half, shrinking as more units are added
take_what: 'zone of control' as an explicit stat: a tile's effective threat/capture radius is inversely proportional to how many friendly tiles already contest that space — one isolated tower threatens everything nearby, but a crowded cluster's marginal tile adds little new territory, which rewards spreading first and consolidating later
constraint: would need to be expressed through Limen's existing adjacent-influence math rather than a new stat, e.g. bonus effective influence for tiles bordering more empty/enemy hexes than friendly ones

name: Dota Underlords positioning guide — Knights cube formation & Drow range (BlueStacks)
one_line: Concrete synergy-shape example: Knights want a literal 3x3 cube block; Drow buffs allies within 1 square
take_what: synergy bonuses tied to a specific GEOMETRIC SHAPE (3x3 block) rather than just 'adjacent count' gives placement a puzzle-piece feel — the player is solving a shape-fitting problem, not just a threshold-counting one
constraint: none — maps cleanly onto Limen's hex tiles as a rare card effect ('bonus if you own all 6 hexes surrounding this tile' i.e. a full ring)

name: TFT targeting mechanics roundup (search synthesis, sourced from Tacter/Mobalytics)
one_line: Catalog of non-default targeting patterns (nearest, farthest, lowest-HP-in-range, furthest-from-center) that individual champions use to break the frontline/backline default
take_what: varied targeting rules per unit type (nearest / farthest / lowest-effective-influence-in-radius) turn positioning into a rock-paper-scissors meta instead of one dominant strategy — e.g. a hypothetical 'flank' keyword unit that must capture the farthest-placed enemy tile rather than the weakest one would force spread-out defense
constraint: Limen already has flank/menace keywords per the brief; this suggests giving 1-2 more keywords an explicit TARGETING RULE (must capture farthest, or lowest-influence-in-2-hex-radius) rather than just a stat modifier

name: r/CompetitiveTFT-style bait/trap corner discussion (via TFT Ninja synthesis)
one_line: Bait-unit tactic: sacrifice a cheap tanky unit in a back corner specifically to lure assassins away from the real carry
take_what: a deliberately 'wrong-looking' placement (weak unit alone in the danger zone) that reads as a bait/decoy for the opponent's aggressive removal — gives positioning a bluffing dimension on top of pure math
constraint: Limen's capture rule (any <=0-influence tile capturable from anywhere) already rewards overextension punishment; adding an explicit 'decoy' card/keyword that looks capturable but retaliates would reinforce this without new systems

name: Auto-Battling Your Way to Victory is Not a Good Design (Jeff Witt, Medium/ggDigest)
one_line: Critique essay arguing hands-off autobattle combat removes player agency once positioning/drafting phase ends
take_what: warns that once setup phase ends and combat auto-resolves, players become spectators to their own decisions for the whole fight duration — the 'wow' moment has to land in the SETUP phase itself (placement, draft) since there is no more agency to feel afterward
constraint: directly relevant to Limen's 'no wow moment' problem: since Limen has NO separate auto-resolve combat phase at all (capture is instant on placement), the fix is to make the capture MOMENT itself (the instant a tile flips to <=0 and gets sniped from anywhere) the spectacle beat, not defer juice to a fight animation
